sections.heading: Error identifiers
sections.text:
AUTH-104 means {{errors.AUTH-104}}. AUTH-140 means {{errors.AUTH-140}}. AUTH-141 means {{errors.AUTH-141}}. The similar identifiers describe different decisions. Reissuing an otherwise identical token can resolve expiry but cannot add a missing scope or move the credential to another workspace.

Use the request identifier when reporting an error. The numeric suffix is not a severity score and must not be compared numerically. A user interface that displays only authentication failed discards the distinction needed to repair the request.

sections.heading: Other failures
sections.text:
RATE-201 means {{errors.RATE-201}}. HOOK-310 means {{errors.HOOK-310}}. DATA-422 means {{errors.DATA-422}}. An HTTP status is a broad category; the Orbit identifier names the product rule that failed. A request with an expired token can be rejected before any measurement validation occurs. Fixing one error can reveal a different validation error on the next attempt.

Do not retry every 4xx response with the same payload. Record the identifier, workspace and timestamp, remove credentials from the log, and select a repair appropriate to the failed rule.
